title: From Structured Records to Patient Narratives: Preserving Clinical Alignment in LLM-Generated Health Summaries
abstract: arXiv:2610.31467v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As wearable and digital health systems increasingly generate longitudinal physiological records, communicating these observations in patient-accessible language remains a significant challenge. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising mechanism for translating structured clinical information into readable narratives, but this process may introduce semantic drift, where clinically precise meaning is distorted during simplification. We investigate evidence-grounded health summarization for menstrual health monitoring using a constrained generation framework that combines structured evidence conditioning with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) using a prompt-based constrained generation framework. We evaluate semantic alignment using Natural Language Inference (NLI), atomic factuality metrics, and readability measures. Across three LLMs and 4,500 generated summaries, explicit grounding constraints consistently improve clinical align

translated_title: 从结构化记录到患者叙事：在大语言模型生成的健康摘要中保持临床一致性
translated_abstract: 随着可穿戴设备和数字健康系统日益产生纵向生理记录，如何用患者易于理解的语言传达这些观测结果仍然是一个重大挑战。大语言模型（LLM）为将结构化临床信息转化为可读的叙事提供了有前景的机制，但这一过程可能引入语义漂移，即在简化过程中临床上的精确含义被扭曲。我们针对月经健康监测研究了基于证据的健康摘要生成，采用一种基于提示的约束生成框架，将结构化证据条件化与检索增强生成（RAG）相结合。我们使用自然语言推理（NLI）、原子事实性指标和可读性度量来评估语义对齐。在三个大语言模型和4,500份生成的摘要中，显式的证据约束持续改善了临床一致性。
tldr: 本文提出一种将结构化证据条件化与检索增强生成（RAG）相结合的提示约束生成框架，用于月经健康监测的可读摘要生成，并通过NLI、原子事实性和可读性评估证明，显式证据约束能够持续提升大语言模型生成摘要的临床语义一致性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a prompt-based constrained generation framework combining structured evidence conditioning with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for readable menstrual health summaries, demonstrating across three LLMs and 4,500 generated summaries that explicit grounding constraints consistently improve clinical alignment.
